newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Telstra banned from misleading ads.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Telstra banned from misleading ads.

text.p: Australian government-owned Telstra Corp has been banned by the Federal Court from making false and misleading advertising, anti-monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said.
ACCC said on Monday the injunction follows ACCC action and Telstra will be restrained by it until December 31, 1999.
The proceedings were brought after Telstra represented that Telstra offered 21 cent local telephone calls, when it was not the case, ACCC said.
The statements were made on television and radio programmes in response to rival Optus's launch of its 20 cent local call.

The ACCC said Telstra referred to its local call saver 15 Flexi-Plan (CS15) but falsely stated its effect. Under CS15 Telstra offers a 15 percent discount on calls which are made within a bracket of A$15 and A$100 per month.
The standard charge by Telstra fo local calls is 25 cents.
ACCC said there is no point at which Telstra customers obtain 21 cent local calls.
Telstra had a monopoly on Australia's A$5.00 billion local call market until June 1996, when Optus Vision launched its local telephony services in tandem with its pay television services.
Optus Vision is owned 46.5 percent by Optus Communications Pty Ltd, which offers international calls.
